title: IaC CI pipeline integrity watchdog and drift-safe rollbacks
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Overview: Build an "integrity watchdog" that augments our existing Terraform CI pipeline to catch and remediate VPC/Private deployment regressions earlier. The watchdog is a lightweight orchestrator that runs alongside plan/apply jobs and performs additional checks (network reachability probes, module compatibility validation, policy evaluation, and drift detection) before and after an apply. It also automates safe rollback PRs and creates clear remediation tasks when automatic rollback is unsafe.

Goals:
- Prevent risky applies to private/VPC deployments by surfacing infra-level failures earlier in CI.
- Enforce policy-as-code checks with richer context (resource graph + last-known-state) and provide actionable policy failures.
- Provide an automated rollback mechanism for a subset of failures and a human-review escalation path for others.
- Record per-change health checks as structured artifacts for the Console (linkable from rollout dashboards).

Scope (what this ticket delivers):
- A CI-side watchdog component (Go service + small container image) integrated into our GitHub Actions/Tekton runner flow.
- Pre-apply network probe step that validates key VPC connectivity assumptions (e.g., route table attachment, subnet CIDR overlap, peering DNS resolution) against a test harness derived from the target workspace.
- Policy evaluation adapter that runs OPA/rego and Conftest-style checks with the Terraform resource graph as input instead of simple JSON plans.
- Post-apply drift probe that checks critical resources (subnet allocations, route tables, NAT gateways) and flags divergence.
- Safe rollback flow: when post-apply probes fail with known-safe signatures (e.g., failed route propagation, NAT provisioning race), the watchdog will open a rollback PR against the same branch using pinned module versions; for unknown failures it will create a detailed incident ticket and attach logs.

Out-of-scope for this ticket:
- Cross-account drift remediation (future).
- Stateful automated migration of DB endpoints (requires app-level coordination).

Design notes:
- The watchdog runs as a short-lived pod/container inside the CI job; it consumes the terraform plan JSON + state snapshot (sanitized) and runs analysis hooks. Hooks implemented: network_probe, resource_graph_validator, policy_runner, post_apply_diff.
- Policy runner: converts resource graph -> OPA input, runs rego bundles from our policy repo (policies/infra/), and returns structured failures with recommended fixes. This layer will also record policy metadata to an artifact JSON for Console ingestion.
- Rollback PR flow: uses our infra tooling (infra/cli) to generate a patch that pins modules to the last-known-good commit (per-state tagging). The watchdog will create a branch rollback/ENG-324119/<short> and open a GH PR with the reason and logs.
- Secrets & access: the watchdog only receives minimal credentials scoped to plan/apply workspaces; it never stores raw state in CI logs. State snapshots are scrubbed (AWS account IDs partially masked).

Acceptance criteria:
- New pipeline step added to terraform/workflows/ that invokes watchdog for all private/VPC workspace applies.
- For 3 synthetic failure scenarios (route table race, subnet CIDR collision, missing IGW), the pipeline: (a) fails fast pre-apply for detectables, or (b) produces a rollback PR for safe post-apply failures.
- Policy runner executes the full rego bundle and surfaces at least 5 policy violations with remediation suggestions in the CI artifact.
- Console shows the watchdog artifact in the rollout timeline for an example deployment (manual verification).

Rollout plan:
- Phase A (canary): enable on a single internal customer workspace (team-rt) and block auto-apply; run in enforcement=report mode for 1 week.
- Phase B: enable enforcement for internal workspaces with automated rollback allowed for known-safe signatures.
- Phase C: expand to customer-facing private workspaces and monitor for 2 weeks before full enforcement.

Observability & telemetry:
- Emit structured logs (json) to infra-logs with tags: workspace, plan_id, watchdog-hook, result.
- Create telemetry counters for policy_failures_by_rule, rollback_attempts, rollback_success_rate.
- Attach artifacts (plan.json, sanitized_state.json, probe_report.json) to the GH run for debugging.

Security considerations:
- Require security review prior to Phase B. Watchdog will not run with elevated privileges by default. Use short-lived ephemeral creds and KMS-encrypted snapshots.

Implementation tasks (high level):
1) Implement watchdog service with pluggable hooks (network_probe, policy_runner, post_apply_diff).
2) Add CI integration and a feature flag in infra/ci-config to opt into watchdog per-workspace.
3) Add rego bundle entrypoints and improve policy messages to include remediation hints.
4) Implement rollback PR generator and verify signatures for safe triggers.
5) Write tests: unit tests for policy adapter, e2e against a mocked AWS sandbox, and synthetic CI runs.

Notes about uniqueness: This approach focuses on combining graph-based policy evaluation, proactive network probes, and an automated-but-conservative rollback PR flow rather than simply failing plan/apply on policy errors.
